Static regression fixtures for the three JS.Agent HTML samples.

The positive fixtures preserve sample bytes with neutral filenames. Controls
remove the appended-document boundary, ActiveX object, or FPU decoder, or retain
only ordinary frame loading, stream use, or packed string growth. The controls
with removed attack legs remain malicious fragments; they are near misses for
these specific composites, not claims of benign identity.

The generic fragmented-ProgID objective was removed in favor of the existing
ActiveX constructor capability. Its four local consumers and the fragmented
msiexec composite now reference that atom. The capability preserves the source
map exclusion and admits the former HTML/JS/Scala/Elixir scope. This fixes a
matcher that asserted ActiveX identity from unrelated string concatenation.

No URL, cookie name, collector filename, or exact file size gates conviction.
The packed-word fingerprints describe x86 decoder instructions, not campaign
configuration. Hidden local pages in the encoded router were not supplied;
findings describe routing and never assert their absent exploit payloads.
